doc.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Joining the union as a teenager
summary: His father, a charter member of the black Philadelphia local, put him in; the union rarely helped with work.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: When did you join the union? Did you join when you joined Les Hite’s band? Or even earlier?
Oh, no. I had been in the union. My father put me in when I was a kid.
Really? Because he was in the union, I guess.
My father was already – he was a charter member of the union in Philadelphia.
Yeah. It was – I think 274 was the number. They had two separate locals in Philadelphia, a white local and a black local. He put me in. I guess I must have been 15 or 16 years old.
Did it help? Did the union help in any ways? Like in a situation like this.

Not really, no. It might have helped me in Philadelphia, in that I could play in some of the places I played in with those bands, and I didn’t have a problem. But as far as helping you get work or anything like that, I’ve never known them to do that.
